mechanism_narrative: Sustained monthly payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 0.3% signals robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with PAYEMS growth exceeding 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeding 2.0% annually indicates aggressive monetary tightening that increases discount rates and depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In FEDFUNDS > 2.0% periods, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate synchronized manufacturing and construction expansion, boosting economic growth and corporate profits for positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Joint INDPRO/HOUST growth fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of instances over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising), declining industrial production (INDPRO) signals economic slowdown that triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25% in past 3 months
failure_condition: In FEDFUNDS-rising periods, INDPRO decline fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeding 2.0% annualized indicates strong economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In GDPC1 growth > 2.0% quarters, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Payroll growth (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% month-over-month signals rapid labor market tightening that accelerates consumer spending, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM months, S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 2.5% annually signals persistent inflation that may trigger aggressive rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In CPIAUCSL inflation > 2.5% periods, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales growth (RSAFS) exceeding 0.4% month-over-month indicates robust consumer demand that supports corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In RSAFS growth > 0.4% MoM months, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances.
